title: Minimum chromatic number for girth-g graphs failing robust orientability

problemStatement.formal: Study the minimum chromatic number of girth-g graphs failing robust orientability, separating rank-based robust orientation from the classical path-based notion.
problemStatement.plain: For graphs of girth g that fail robust orientability in the classical sense, what chromatic number is forced, and where is the bound sharp?
whyMatters: This is the main Erdos1006 chromatic-number scaffold and explains the FFLLW lower-bound threshold.

proven: Rank-based robust orientation follows from colorability, so every finite graph has one in the rank-based setup.
K3 is formalized as a girth-3 classical witness with chromatic number 3 and no classically robust orientation.
Several rank-based lower-bound statements are proved, some vacuously because every finite graph is rank-based robust.
open: The general classical FFLLW lower bound remains represented by `ffllw_classical`.
knownResults.goal: Keep the chromatic-number scaffold clear about rank-based versus classical robust orientation.

currentState.focus: Graduated chromatic-number scaffold refreshed: current metadata now includes the seven-file Erdos1006 family and explicitly separates rank-based results from the classical FFLLW axiom.
currentState.nextAction: No metadata action; future Lean work should either reduce `ffllw_classical` or move classical robustness facts into narrower child slugs.

knowledge.progressSummary: Metadata sync 2026-05-18: Erdos1006OQ02.lean script-counts as 470 lines, 17 theorems, 1 axiom, 8 definitions, and 1 raw sorry hit from comment text. The file proves rank-based robustness results and K3 classical witness facts while keeping the general classical FFLLW lower bound as an axiom.
builtItems: coloringOrientation and rank-based robust orientation lemmas.
insights: Rank-based robust acyclicity collapses to a very broad existence result for finite graphs.
Classical path-based robustness is the setting where the FFLLW girth/chromatic threshold remains meaningful.
nextSteps: Reduce or localize the `ffllw_classical` axiom if future classical-robustness work resumes.
